newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end sharply higher on bull spreads.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end sharply higher on bull spreads.

text.p: CBOT old crop soybean futures ended sharply higher on Wednesday, bolstered by aggressive bull spreading amid signals the market was oversold and reports of export business, traders said.

"It was a day of bull spreading," said Bob Lekberg, analyst with Goldenberg-Hehmeyer. "We were just on too steep a decline and the fundamentals still say we have a tight carryover. Farmers are not doing much selling of beans, there's no room for weather trouble here at all."
Reports Brazil and Argentina were buying U.S. new crop soybeans lifted new crop months, traders said.

Argentine traders said Argentina bought two cargoes of new crop U.S. soybeans. CBOT sources cited talk that the 150,000 tonnes of new crop soybeans that USDA reported sold to unknown on Tuesday were purchased by a Brazilian processor.

The sharp premium for spot shipment made it profitable for South American exporters to sell now and buy lower-priced U.S. new crop supplies in the fall, traders said. July futures gained roughly 14 cents a bushel on new crop November and the spread closed at $1.79-3/4, premium July.
Soybeans ended 18-1/4 to two cents per bushel higher with July up 18-1/4 at $8.49-1/2 a bushel.

Technically, the soybean market appeared to be oversold and due for a correction, traders said. They pointed to the bullish concensus for May 27 which fell to 47 percent from 65 percent. Traders said the drop was exaggerated and did not reflect continued bullish fundamental factors.

The July contract briefly topped the 10-day moving average level of $8.50-3/4 per bushel before closing just shy of that mark. Chartists said that contract would test the $8.54 level next and needed to close above $8.57-1/2 to confirm a bullish trend.

Spread trading was the featured action on the day. Pit sources said Continental Grain bull spread four million bushels July/November on the close which contributed to the sharp spread move. The spread closed at $1.79-1/2, premium July, the widest close since May 7 when it ended at $1.84.
LIT spread one million July/November at $1.68-1/2 to $1.69, premium July and Prudential Securities spread one million November/July at $1.68-1/2.

On the day, funds bought at least 10 million bushels, led by Rosenthal Collins with five million July. Term Commodities bought five million August and Tenco Inc bought three million November, pit sources said.
In options, Rand Financial bought 700 July $8.50 calls at 14 to 15-1/4 cents, CIS sold 300 November $6.00 puts at 10 cents and ING sold 250 August $9.00 calls at seven cents.
Soybean futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 75,000 contracts, compared with Tuesday's actual volume of 88,207.
